correctness.rationale: Resultant_y(F,G)=x^9 and F_y(0,0,1)=1 prove the unique length-nine base point. Gröbner reductions of the full finite Jacobian ideal in char2 give (x,y+t,t³+1), and char3 (x−y²,y³−1,t); homogeneous derivatives exclude singular support at infinity. The char2 tangent cone x²+txv+t²v² has branch directions governed by u²+u+1, split over F_{2^r} iff r even; at t=∞ the tangent is xy and split. In char3 at (1,1,1), the exact local equation w²+w v²−v³=0 is A2 cusp; the other singularity is a split node. Normalization P1 gives q+2/q/q+1 point counts. Hasse invariants are t (char2) and t² (char3); the discriminant of the projection quartic is −256(t³+27), I=t(t³+24), implying j(C_t)=−t^9 in char3. Independent exact resultants, Jacobian systems over F2/F3, Hasse coefficient, quartic discriminant, and prime-field projective singular sets corroborated.
